samples.question: The picture shows exactly one pale card on a light page, and the card is filled with straight dark bars. Every pale grey blob outside the card is background clutter and must be ignored. All bars have the same dark colour and the same thickness, they all run in the same direction, and they are spaced by one constant pitch, where a pitch means the distance from one bar to the next bar; so colour, thickness, bar count, card position, card size and the total amount of dark ink say nothing about the answer. Somewhere inside the card there is exactly one triangular patch in which the bars are shifted sideways, across the bars, by exactly half a pitch, so that inside the patch the bars sit in the gaps of the bars outside it. Nothing else marks that patch: it has no outline, no colour of its own and no extra ink, and it can be seen only where the bars fail to line up along its border. The patch is a triangle with two equal sides, so it has one straight side, its base, and one opposite corner, its tip, and the tip points straight up, straight down, straight left or straight right on the page. Report the direction in which the tip of the patch points. Answer unclear if the patch is too small to read, that is if either its base or its depth from base to tip spans fewer than about four pitches. Which way does the tip of the shifted patch point: up, down, left, right, or unclear?
